Interprets `max_mem_mb >= allocated_mem_mb` (`Runtime.ExitError`) as a Lambda Out-Of-Memory crash and recommends increasing `MemorySize` (noting that Lambda proportionally increases vCPU and network throughput with memory)

evals.prompt: Our ECS Fargate service `payments-worker` in `ap-south-1` has two failure modes across tasks: (1) Task `t-111` exited with `stoppedReason: "OutOfMemoryError: Container killed due to memory usage"` and `exitCode: 137` on a Node.js 20 container (`memory: 1024`), and (2) Task `t-222` in a private subnet failed to start with `CannotPullContainerError: pull image manifest has been retried 5 time(s): failed to do request: Head https://123456789012.dkr.ecr.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/v2/...: i/o timeout` even though we already created Interface VPC Endpoints for `ecr.api` and `ecr.dkr`! Diagnose both failures and provide the exact fixes.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses (1) `ExitCode: 137` (`SIGKILL` OOM) by increasing task/container `memory` in the ECS Task Definition and setting `NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=768"` (~75% of container memory so V8 GC runs before the Linux OOM killer), and (2) `CannotPullContainerError` timeout by explaining that ECR stores actual image layers in Amazon S3 (requiring an **S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint** `com.amazonaws.ap-south-1.s3` on the private route table in addition to `ecr.api` and `ecr.dkr`, plus checking whether `assignPublicIp: ENABLED` was mistakenly set in a private subnet without an IGW or `kms:Decrypt` is missing on `executionRoleArn`).
expectations: Explains that `ExitCode: 137` (`128 + 9` `SIGKILL`) with `OutOfMemoryError` means the Linux kernel cgroup OOM killer terminated the container, and fixes it by increasing Task Definition `memory` and setting `NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=..."` (or `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS="-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75.0"`)

Explains why `CannotPullContainerError` still times out when only `ecr.api` and `ecr.dkr` Interface VPC Endpoints exist: ECR stores container image layers in Amazon S3, so a private subnet without a NAT Gateway also requires the **S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint** (`com.amazonaws.ap-south-1.s3`) in its route table

Also checks the two other `CannotPullContainerError` culprits: `assignPublicIp: ENABLED` on a task in a private subnet (causing traffic to route to a non-existent IGW) and missing `AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy` / `kms:Decrypt` on `executionRoleArn`

evals.prompt: Our Lambda function (`Timeout: 60` seconds, `BatchSize: 10`) polls an SQS queue (`VisibilityTimeout: 30` seconds, no `RedrivePolicy`). Whenever 1 poison message fails in a batch of 10, all 10 messages are retried repeatedly and duplicate orders are processed! Provide the complete architectural and IaC fix for the SQS queue, Lambda Event Source Mapping (ESM), and handler return format.
evals.expected_output: Identifies three bugs and fixes them: (1) `VisibilityTimeout` (`30s`) is shorter than `FunctionTimeout` (`60s`), causing SQS to make in-flight messages visible to other consumers before the Lambda finishes — sets `VisibilityTimeout >= 6 * FunctionTimeout` (`>= 360` seconds), (2) enables `FunctionResponseTypes: ["ReportBatchItemFailures"]` on the Event Source Mapping and returns `{"batchItemFailures": [{"itemIdentifier": message["messageId"}]}` from the handler so only failed messages retry, and (3) attaches a Dead-Letter Queue (`RedrivePolicy` with `maxReceiveCount: 3` to `5`) plus a CloudWatch alarm on DLQ `ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible > 0`.
expectations: Fixes the SQS `VisibilityTimeout` by setting `VisibilityTimeout >= 6 * FunctionTimeout` (`>= 360` seconds for a `60s` Lambda) and explains why `30s < 60s` caused duplicate concurrent processing of in-flight messages

Enables `FunctionResponseTypes: ["ReportBatchItemFailures"]` on the `AWS::Lambda::EventSourceMapping` and shows the handler returning `{"batchItemFailures": [{"itemIdentifier": "<messageId>"}]}` so successful records in the batch are deleted while only failed records retry
Attaches a Dead-Letter Queue (`RedrivePolicy` with `deadLetterTargetArn` and `maxReceiveCount`) to isolate poison-pill messages

evals.prompt: Explain the security difference between an ECS Fargate `executionRoleArn` (Task Execution Role) and `taskRoleArn` (Task Role), why putting application S3/DynamoDB permissions on `executionRoleArn` or passing database passwords in plaintext `environment` variables is dangerous, and how `secrets` (`valueFrom`) injection works.
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes `executionRoleArn` (used by the ECS container agent/Fargate control plane to pull ECR images, push `awslogs` to CloudWatch, and fetch Secrets Manager/SSM secrets at container startup) from `taskRoleArn` (assumed by the application code inside the container via `AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI` for S3/DynamoDB/SQS calls), and shows how `secrets` (`valueFrom` referencing a Secrets Manager ARN + `kms:Decrypt` on `executionRoleArn`) avoids exposing credentials in `ecs:DescribeTaskDefinition`.
expectations: Clearly distinguishes `executionRoleArn` (used by the Fargate/ECS agent to pull images from ECR, write logs to CloudWatch, and resolve `secrets` at startup) from `taskRoleArn` (used by the application code running inside the container)

Shows how to inject sensitive credentials via the Task Definition `secrets` block (`name` + `valueFrom: arn:aws:secretsmanager:...`) rather than plaintext `environment` variables, noting that `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` and `kms:Decrypt` belong on `executionRoleArn` for startup injection

evals.prompt: Our Spring Boot container on ECS Fargate takes ~75 seconds to initialize Liquibase migrations on startup, causing the ALB (`HealthCheckIntervalSeconds: 15`, `UnhealthyThresholdCount: 2`) to kill the task every 30 seconds in an endless `Task failed ELB health checks` loop (`healthCheckGracePeriodSeconds: 0`). Fix the health check flapping and configure both ECS Rolling Update circuit breakers and CodeDeploy Canary auto-rollback in IaC.
evals.expected_output: Fixes the startup kill loop by setting `healthCheckGracePeriodSeconds: 120` on the ECS Service and `startPeriod: 90` on the Container `healthCheck` (plus verifying the Task Security Group allows ingress from the ALB Security Group on the container port), and provides IaC for `deploymentCircuitBreaker: { enable: true, rollback: true }` (rolling update) and `AWS::CodeDeploy::DeploymentGroup` (`ECSCanary10Percent5Minutes` + `autoRollbackConfiguration: { enabled: true, events: ["DEPLOYMENT_FAILURE", "DEPLOYMENT_STOP_ON_ALARM"] }`).
expectations: Resolves `Task failed ELB health checks` during slow Spring Boot startup by setting `healthCheckGracePeriodSeconds` (e.g., `120` seconds) on the ECS Service and `healthCheck.startPeriod` on the container definition (while also verifying SG-to-SG ingress from the ALB SG to the Task SG on the container port)
Configures `deploymentCircuitBreaker: { enable: true, rollback: true }` for ECS rolling updates

Configures `AWS::CodeDeploy` progressive rollout (`ECSCanary10Percent5Minutes` or `LambdaCanary10Percent10Minutes`) with `autoRollbackConfiguration: { enabled: true, events: ["DEPLOYMENT_FAILURE", "DEPLOYMENT_STOP_ON_ALARM"] }` wired to CloudWatch `5XX`/`Errors` alarms
